metadata.title: Your IQ Test Narrative: Reading One Reasoning Session
metadata.description: Use four layers and a fictional 18/30 comparison to separate report fields, personal observations, and hypotheses, then choose a reviewable next step.

faq_items.question: Can online IQ test scores be converted to percentiles?
faq_items.answer: A percentile has a meaningful interpretive foundation only when the tool publicly specifies the applicable norms, scoring methodology, and reference group. Percentile conversions should not be performed independently when current public information is insufficient.

faq_items.question: Do You Need to Retake a Test Immediately if the Score is Low?
faq_items.answer: Usually no immediate repetition is needed. First record the environment, question type, and error strategy to avoid mistaking familiarity for greater accuracy.

faq_items.question: Why do I get different scores on different websites?
faq_items.answer: Items, difficulty, scoring, normative data, timed status, and presentation format may differ. Identical names do not imply that results can be directly compared.

faq_items.question: Can we identify specific cognitive deficits from mistakes?
faq_items.answer: Online tests alone cannot diagnose cognitive deficits. Errors can be used for strategic review; when genuine health or academic concerns exist, appropriate professional evaluation should be sought.

faq_items.question: Can Results Predict Learning or Career Success?
faq_items.answer: This online result alone is insufficient for an individual prediction. Outcomes also depend on knowledge, motivation, opportunity, health, resources, collaboration, and long-term behavior.
